motors.label: Budget build: MP8085 on wall power
motors.note: The lowest-cost build, with its own simpler frame: plate and angle bought near size, cut with a hacksaw and drilled through printed guides (no CNC), hung on the rack upright with one hitch pin. The MP8085 sits in an outside pod; an ODESC V4.2 with a fan drives it from a Mean Well 48 V supply in a floor box. A knob, a start/stop button and a phone app (Bluetooth) set the weight: no battery, no screen. 2.0 m of pull. 180 lb is a design target held through a 20-30 s set, not yet verified: it takes about 69 A from the ODESC, whose 70 A rating is the seller's, and the motor's torque against current is still to be bench-tested.
motors.size: About 480 mm across with the motor pod
motors.made: Metal bought near size: a hacksaw, a drill and a printer

motors.label: Main build: MP8085 on battery
motors.note: The main build: the bolted 6061 aluminum frame, about 515 mm long, a 10S battery and the touchscreen. The 7/8 in drum tube is used as bought (no lathe), and every load-bearing screw goes to a nut. 2.6 m of pull. The rack side goes on with one hitch pin and a lever clamp; the unit lifts off with one pull of the latch. 220 lb is a design target held through a 20-30 s set, not yet verified: it takes about 75 A from the ODrive Pro, and the motor's torque against current is still to be bench-tested.

outsourced.name: Laser-cut plate set, 6061-T6
outsourced.note: The base, rear and motor face plates (with their nut windows), the drum flanges and the latch slider (0.250 and 0.375 in), plus the four 2 mm steel bearing cheeks, cut from the DXF files at an instant-priced laser service such as SendCutSend. The prototype's plates came to about $200-300 at SendCutSend (October 2026). Countersinking is extra, charged per hole.

outsourced.name: Thick plate parts: drum holders, corner gussets, rack side and ODrive heatsink
outsourced.note: The two 3/8 in drum bearing holders, the three 1/4 in corner gussets, the rack side's mating plate, its two 1/2 in cheeks and pad bar, and the finned ODrive heatsink, milled from plate (no machined blocks, no lathe). The 28 mm bearing bores are finished to H7.

outsourced.name: Drum tube, 6061-T6, 7/8 in OD x 1/8 in wall, 162 mm
outsourced.note: From a metal supplier such as Metal Supermarkets or Online Metals, cut square (reference: about $8.50 a foot). Used as bought: no lathe.
